verses.text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul travelled through the inland country and arrived at Ephesus. There he found some followers.
He asked them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" They answered, "No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit."
So Paul asked, "Then what baptism did you receive?" They said, "John's baptism."
Paul said, "John's baptism was a baptism for turning away from sin. He told the people to believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Jesus."
When they heard this, they were baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in other languages and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months. He reasoned with the people and tried to persuade them about God's Kingdom.

But some of them became stubborn. They refused to believe and spoke evil of the Way in front of the crowd. So Paul left them. He took the followers with him and talked with people every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that all the Jews and Greeks who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord.
God did amazing miracles through Paul.
Even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick. Their sicknesses were healed, and evil spirits left them.

Some Jews who went around driving out evil spirits tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus over people who had evil spirits. They would say, "In the name of Jesus, whom Paul preaches, I order you to come out."
Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
One day the evil spirit answered them, "I know Jesus, and I know about Paul, but who are you?"
Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He beat them so badly that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
When this became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, they were all filled with fear, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honour.
Many of those who believed now came and openly confessed the evil things they had done.
A number of those who had practised magic brought their books together and burned them in front of everyone. When they added up the value of the books, it came to fifty thousand silver coins.
In this way the word of the Lord spread widely and grew in power.
After all this had happened, Paul decided by the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. "After I have been there," he said, "I must also visit Rome."
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed in Asia a little longer.
About that time there was a great disturbance about the Way.
A silversmith named Demetrius made small silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. His business brought a lot of work to the craftsmen.
He called them together, along with other workers in the same trade, and said, "Men, you know that we earn a good living from this business.

And you see and hear what this man Paul has done. He has persuaded and led astray large numbers of people here in Ephesus and in almost the whole of Asia. He says that gods made by human hands are not gods at all.

There is a danger that our trade will lose its good name. And the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be thought of as nothing. She is worshipped in all of Asia and the whole world, but she will be robbed of her greatness."
When they heard this, they were furious and began shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
Soon the whole city was in an uproar. The people grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's travelling companions from Macedonia, and all rushed together into the theatre.
Paul wanted to go in and speak to the crowd, but the followers would not let him.
Even some officials of the province, who were friends of Paul, sent him a message begging him not to go into the theatre.
The meeting was in confusion. Some people were shouting one thing and some another. Most of them did not even know why they were there.
The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander to the front, and some of the crowd told him what to say. He waved his hand for silence because he wanted to defend himself before the people.
But when they realised he was a Jew, they all shouted together for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
The city clerk calmed the crowd and said, "People of Ephesus, everyone knows that the city of Ephesus guards the temple of the great Artemis, and her image that fell from heaven.
No one can deny these facts. So you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
You have brought these men here, though they have not robbed temples or said evil things about our goddess.
If Demetrius and his craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and there are governors. They can bring charges there.
If there is anything more you want to bring up, it must be settled in a lawful meeting.
As it is, we are in danger of being charged with rioting because of what happened today. There is no reason for it, and we would not be able to explain this uproar."
After he had said this, he sent the crowd away.
